readings.title: Fasting for the Cosmic Verdict
readings.subtitle: Dani’ěl physically starves the flesh to align with the impending revelation of geopolitical shifts.
readings.text: [Daniel 10:1] In the third year of Koresh sovereign of Persia a word was revealed to Dani’ěl, whose name was called Bělteshatstsar. And the word was true, and the conflict great. And he understood the word, and had understanding of the vision. [2] In those days <dn>I</dn>, Dani’ěl, was mourning three weeks of days. [3] <dn>I</dn> did not eat desirable food, and meat and wine did not come into <dn>my</dn> mouth, and <dn>I</dn> did not anoint <dn>myself</dn> at all, till the completion of three weeks of days.

readings.title: The Man Clothed in Linen
readings.subtitle: Dani’ěl is overwhelmed by the hyper-dense, uncontained light of the divine emissary.
readings.text: [4] And on the twenty-fourth day of the first new moon, while <dn>I</dn> was by the side of the great river, that is Ḥiddeqel, [5] then <dn>I</dn> lifted <dn>my</dn> eyes and looked and saw a certain man dressed in linen, whose loins were girded with gold of Uphaz! [6] And <dn>his</dn> body was like beryl, and <dn>his</dn> face like the appearance of lightning, and <dn>his</dn> eyes like torches of fire, and <dn>his</dn> arms and feet like polished bronze in appearance, and the sound of <dn>his</dn> words like the sound of a crowd. [7] And <dn>I</dn>, Dani’ěl, alone saw the vision, for the men who were with me did not see the vision, but a great trembling fell upon them, and they ran away to hide themselves. [8] So <dn>I</dn> was left alone when <dn>I</dn> saw this great vision, and no strength remained in me, for <dn>my</dn> comeliness was destroyed in me, and <dn>I</dn> retained no strength. [9] But <dn>I</dn> heard the sound of <dn>his</dn> words. And while <dn>I</dn> heard the sound of <dn>his</dn> words <dn>I</dn> was stunned lying with <dn>my</dn> face to the ground.

readings.title: The Command to Stand Upright
readings.subtitle: A physical touch activates Dani’ěl, shifting him from operational paralysis to active reception.
readings.text: [10] And see, a hand touched me, and set me trembling on <dn>my</dn> knees and on the palms of <dn>my</dn> hands. [11] And <dn>he</dn> said to me, <dq>“O Dani’ěl, man greatly appreciated, understand the words that <dn>I</dn> speak to you, and stand upright, for <dn>I</dn> have now been sent to you.”</dq> And while <dn>he</dn> was speaking this word to me, <dn>I</dn> stood trembling.

readings.title: The Prince of Persia Withstands
readings.subtitle: The messenger reveals a twenty-one-day delay caused by high-level territorial resistance, requiring Miḵa’ěl's direct intervention.
readings.text: [Daniel 10:12] And <dn>he</dn> said to me, <dq>“Do not fear, Dani’ěl, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your <dn>Elohim</dn>, your words were heard, and <dn>I</dn> have come because of your words. [13] “But the head of the rule of Persia withstood me twenty-one days. And see, Miḵa’ěl, one of the chief heads, came to help me, for <dn>I</dn> had been left alone there with the sovereigns of Persia. [14] “And <dn>I</dn> have come to make you understand what is to befall your people in the latter days. For the vision is yet for days to come.”</dq>

readings.title: Strength from the Messenger
readings.subtitle: The physical touch of the messenger restores Dani’ěl’s operational capacity to engage the timeline.
readings.text: [15] And when <dn>he</dn> had spoken such words to me, <dn>I</dn> turned <dn>my</dn> face toward the ground and kept silent. [16] And see, one who looked like the sons of men touched <dn>my</dn> lips, and <dn>I</dn> opened <dn>my</dn> mouth and spoke and said to <dn>him</dn> who stood before me, “<dn>My</dn> master, because of the vision <dn>I</dn> have been seized with pains, and <dn>I</dn> have retained no strength. [17] “So how was this servant of <dn>my</dn> master able to speak with you, <dn>my</dn> master? As for me, no strength remains in me now, nor is any breath left in me.” [18] And again the one who looked like a man touched me and strengthened me. [19] And <dn>he</dn> said, <dq>“Do not fear, O man greatly appreciated! Peace be to you, be strong now, be strong!”</dq> So when <dn>he</dn> spoke to me <dn>I</dn> was strengthened, and said, “Let <dn>my</dn> master speak, for you have strengthened me.”

readings.title: Decrees of the Hellenized Future
readings.subtitle: The messenger prepares to re-engage the adversarial forces driving Persia and Greece.
readings.text: [20] And <dn>he</dn> said, <dq>“Do you know why <dn>I</dn> have come to you? And now <dn>I</dn> return to fight with the head of Persia. And when <dn>I</dn> have left, see, the head of Greece shall come. [21] “But let me declare to you <dn>את</dn> what is written in the Scripture of Truth, and there is not one strengthening <dn>himself</dn> with me concerning these, except Miḵa’ěl your head. [11:1] “And in the first year of Dareyavesh the Mede, <dn>I</dn> <dn>myself</dn> stood up to support and protect <dn>him</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: The Division of Greece
readings.subtitle: The absolute dominion of the mighty sovereign is shattered and scattered to the four winds by divine decree.
readings.text: [Daniel 11:2] <dq>“And now <dn>I</dn> declare the truth to you: See, three more sovereigns are to arise in Persia, and the fourth is to become far richer than them all. And by <dn>his</dn> power, through <dn>his</dn> riches, <dn>he</dn> stirs up all against the rulership of Greece. [3] “And a mighty sovereign shall arise, and <dn>he</dn> shall rule with great authority, and do as <dn>he</dn> pleases. [4] “But when <dn>he</dn> has arisen, <dn>his</dn> rule shall be broken up and divided toward the four winds of the heavens, but not among <dn>his</dn> descendants nor according to <dn>his</dn> authority with which <dn>he</dn> ruled, because <dn>his</dn> rule shall be uprooted, even for others besides these.”</dq>

readings.title: Alliances of the North and South
readings.subtitle: Endless treaties and betrayals map the systemic friction within the adversarial kingdoms.
readings.text: [Daniel 11:5] <dq>“And a sovereign of the South shall become strong, and one of <dn>his</dn> princes; and <dn>he</dn> shall be strong over <dn>him</dn> and shall rule – <dn>his</dn> rule shall be a great rule. [6] “And at the end of years they shall join themselves together, and a daughter of the sovereign of the South shall come to the sovereign of the North to make an alliance. But she shall not retain <dn>את</dn> the strength of her power, nor would <dn>he</dn> or <dn>his</dn> power stand. And she shall be given up, with those who brought her, and <dn>he</dn> who brought her forth, and <dn>he</dn> who supported her in those times. [7] “But from a branch of her roots one shall arise in <dn>his</dn> place, and <dn>he</dn> shall come into the defence and come into a stronghold of the sovereign of the North, and shall act against them, and shall prevail, [8] and also their mighty ones, with their princes and their precious utensils of silver and gold <dn>he</dn> shall seize and bring to Mitsrayim. And <dn>he</dn> shall stand more years than the sovereign of the North. [9] “Then <dn>he</dn> shall enter the reign of the sovereign of the South, but shall return to <dn>his</dn> own land.

readings.title: The Army Overflows
readings.subtitle: The friction accelerates as massive military forces clash without ultimate resolution.
readings.text: [10] “But <dn>his</dn> sons shall stir themselves up, and assemble a great army. And <dn>he</dn> shall certainly come and overflow and pass through, then return to <dn>his</dn> stronghold, and be stirred up. [11] “Then the sovereign of the South shall be enraged and go out to fight with <dn>him</dn>, with the sovereign of the North, who shall raise a large army. But the army shall be given into the hand of <dn>his</dn> enemy, [12] and <dn>he</dn> shall capture the army, <dn>his</dn> heart being exalted. And <dn>he</dn> shall cause tens of thousands to fall, but not prevail.”</dq>

readings.title: Standing in the Splendid Land
readings.subtitle: The sovereign of the North asserts regional dominance, bringing destruction to the covenant land.
readings.text: [Daniel 11:13] <dq>“And the sovereign of the North shall return and raise an army greater than the former, and certainly come at the end of some years with a great army and much supplies. [14] “And in those times many shall rise up against the sovereign of the South, while some violent ones among your people exalt themselves to establish the vision, but they shall stumble. [15] “Then the sovereign of the North shall come in and build a siege mound, and capture a city of strongholds. And the arms of the South shall not stand, nor <dn>his</dn> choice people, for there is no strength to stand. [16] “So <dn>his</dn> opponent shall do as <dn>he</dn> pleases – with no one standing against <dn>him</dn> – and stand in the Splendid Land with destruction in <dn>his</dn> hand.

readings.title: The Imposition on the Adorned City
readings.subtitle: A ruler extracts wealth through systemic debt but is swiftly removed from the timeline.
readings.text: [17] “And <dn>he</dn> shall set <dn>his</dn> face to enter with the strength of <dn>his</dn> entire rule, and make an alliance with <dn>him</dn>. And <dn>he</dn> shall do so, and give <dn>him</dn> <dn>את</dn> the daughter of women to corrupt her. But she shall not stand, neither be for <dn>him</dn>. [18] “Then <dn>he</dn> shall turn <dn>his</dn> face to the coastlands and capture many. But a ruler shall bring the reproach against them to an end. And with the reproach removed, <dn>he</dn> shall turn back on <dn>him</dn>. [19] “Then <dn>he</dn> shall turn <dn>his</dn> face toward the strongholds of <dn>his</dn> own land, but shall stumble and fall, and not be found. [20] “And in <dn>his</dn> place one shall stand up who imposes taxes on the adorned city of the rule, but within a few days <dn>he</dn> is destroyed, but not in wrath or in battle.”</dq>

readings.title: Seizing Power Through Flatteries
readings.subtitle: A despised entity subverts the covenant and initiates deceitful economic plundering.
readings.text: [Daniel 11:21] <dq>“And in <dn>his</dn> place shall arise a despised one, to whom they shall not give the excellency of the rule. But <dn>he</dn> shall come in peaceably, and seize the rule by flatteries. [22] “And the arms of the flood shall be swept away from before <dn>him</dn> and be broken, and also the prince of the covenant. [23] “And after they joined <dn>him</dn>, <dn>he</dn> shall work deceit, and shall come up and become strong with a small nation. [24] “<dn>He</dn> shall enter peaceably, even into the richest places of the province, and do what <dn>his</dn> fathers have not done, nor <dn>his</dn> forefathers: distribute among them plunder and spoil and supplies, and devise <dn>his</dn> plots against the strongholds, but only for a time.

readings.title: Hearts Against the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Political plots are devised, and the sovereign's heart firmly aligns against YeHoVaH's set-apart covenant.
readings.text: [25] “And <dn>he</dn> shall stir up <dn>his</dn> power and <dn>his</dn> heart against the sovereign of the South with a great army, and the sovereign of the South shall be stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army, but not stand, for they shall devise plots against <dn>him</dn>. [26] “And those who have been eating <dn>his</dn> food shall destroy <dn>him</dn>, and <dn>his</dn> army be swept away, and many fall down slain. [27] “And both these sovereigns’ hearts are to do evil, and speak lies at the same table, but not prosper, for the end is still for an appointed time. [28] “Then <dn>he</dn> shall return to <dn>his</dn> land with much supplies, and <dn>his</dn> heart be against the set-apart covenant. And <dn>he</dn> shall act, and shall return to <dn>his</dn> land.

readings.title: Halting the Continual Offerings
readings.subtitle: The set-apart place is profaned, and those holding to Torah are refined through extreme adversarial fire.
readings.text: [29] “At the appointed time <dn>he</dn> shall return and go toward the south, but it shall not be like the former or the latter. [30] “For ships from Kittim shall come against <dn>him</dn>, and <dn>he</dn> shall lose heart, and shall return in rage against the set-apart covenant, and shall act, and shall return and consider those who forsake the set-apart covenant. [31] “And strong ones shall arise from <dn>him</dn> and profane the set-apart place, the stronghold, and shall take away <dn>את</dn> that which is continual, and set up the abomination that lays waste. [32] “And by flatteries <dn>he</dn> shall profane those who do wrong against the covenant, but the people who know their <dn>Elohim</dn> shall be strong, and shall act. [33] “And those of the people who have insight shall give understanding to many. And they shall stumble by sword and flame, by captivity and plundering, for days. [34] “And when they stumble, they shall be helped, a little help, but many shall join them, by flatteries. [35] “And some of those who have insight shall stumble, to refine them, and to cleanse them, and to make them white, until the time of the end, for it is still for an appointed time.”</dq>

readings.title: The Willful Sovereign's Hubris
readings.subtitle: A geopolitical leader demands ultimate compliance, funding strongholds with the extracted wealth of nations.
readings.text: [Daniel 11:36] <dq>“And the sovereign shall do as <dn>he</dn> pleases, and exalt <dn>himself</dn> and show <dn>himself</dn> to be great above every mighty one, and speak incredible matters against the <dn>Ěl</dn> of mighty ones, and shall prosper until the wrath has been accomplished – for what has been decreed shall be done – [37] and have no regard for the mighty ones of <dn>his</dn> fathers nor for the desire of women, nor have regard for any mighty one, but exalt <dn>himself</dn> above them all. [38] “But in <dn>his</dn> place <dn>he</dn> shall give esteem to a mighty one of strongholds. And to a mighty one which <dn>his</dn> fathers did not know <dn>he</dn> shall give esteem with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts. [39] “And <dn>he</dn> shall act against the strongest strongholds with a foreign mighty one, which <dn>he</dn> shall acknowledge. <dn>He</dn> shall increase in esteem and cause them to rule over many, and divide the land for gain.

readings.title: Pitching Tents Between the Seas
readings.subtitle: The final adversarial push surrounds the set-apart mountain before its divinely mandated annihilation.
readings.text: [40] “At the time of the end the sovereign of the South shall push at <dn>him</dn>, and the sovereign of the North rush against <dn>him</dn> like a whirlwind, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships. And <dn>he</dn> shall enter the lands, and shall overflow and pass over, [41] and shall enter the Splendid Land, and many shall stumble, but these escape from <dn>his</dn> hand: Eḏom, and Mo’aḇ, and the chief of the sons of Ammon. [42] “And <dn>he</dn> shall stretch out <dn>his</dn> hand against the lands, and the land of Mitsrayim shall not escape. [43] “And <dn>he</dn> shall rule over the treasures of gold and silver, and over all the riches of Mitsrayim, and Libyans and Kushites shall be at <dn>his</dn> steps. [44] “Then reports from the east and the north shall disturb <dn>him</dn>, and <dn>he</dn> shall go out with great wrath to destroy and put many under the ban, [45] and <dn>he</dn> shall pitch the tents of <dn>his</dn> palace between the seas and the splendid set-apart mountain, but shall come to <dn>his</dn> end with none to help <dn>him</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: Miḵa’ěl Stands Up
readings.subtitle: At the peak of terrestrial distress, the Right Arm executes the premial reward of resurrection for the covenant people.
readings.text: [Daniel 12:1] <dq>“Now at that time Miḵa’ěl shall stand up, the great head who is standing over the sons of your people. And there shall be a time of distress, such as never was since there was a nation, until that time. And at that time your people shall be delivered, every one who is found written in the book, [2] and many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth wake up, some to everlasting life, and some to reproaches, everlasting abhorrence. [3] “And those who have insight shall shine like the brightness of the expanse, and those who lead many to righteousness like the stars forever and ever. [4] “But you, Dani’ěl, hide the words, and seal the book until the time of the end. Many shall diligently search and knowledge shall increase.”</dq>

readings.title: The Oath Above the Waters
readings.subtitle: A strict timeline is established for the shattering of the set-apart people's power before the final restoration.
readings.text: [Daniel 12:5] Then <dn>I</dn>, Dani’ěl, looked and saw two others standing, one on this bank of the river and the other on that bank. [6] And one said to the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long until the end of these wonders?” [7] And <dn>I</dn> heard the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, and <dn>he</dn> held up <dn>his</dn> right hand and <dn>his</dn> left hand to the heavens, and swore by <dn>Him</dn> who lives forever, that it would be for an appointed time, appointed times, and half a time. And when they have ended scattering the power of the set-apart people, then all these shall be completed. [8] And <dn>I</dn> heard, but <dn>I</dn> did not understand, so <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>My</dn> master, what is the latter end of these matters?”

readings.title: The 1,335 Days
readings.subtitle: The mathematical calendar is sealed; Dani’ěl is commanded to rest until his ultimate inheritance at the end of days.
readings.text: [9] And <dn>he</dn> said, <dq>“Go, Dani’ěl, for the words are hidden and sealed till the time of the end. [10] “Many shall be cleansed and made white, and refined. But the wrong shall do wrong – and none of the wrong shall understand, but those who have insight shall understand. [11] “And from the time that which is continual is taken away, and the abomination that lays waste is set up, is one thousand two hundred and ninety days. [12] “Blessed is he who is waiting earnestly, and comes to the one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days. [13] “But you, go your way till the end. And rest, and arise to your lot at the end of the days.”</dq>

readings.title: The Prophets Activate the Remnant
readings.subtitle: Ḥaggai and Zeḵaryah inject the words of YeHoVaH into the paralyzed builders, commanding the work to resume.
readings.text: [Ezra 4:24] Then the work of the House of Elah which is at Yerushalayim ceased, and it ceased until the second year of the reign of Dareyavesh sovereign of Persia. [5:1] Then the prophets, Ḥaggai the prophet and Zeḵaryah son of Iddo, prophesied to the Yehuḏim who were in Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, in the Name of the Elah of Yisra’ěl upon them.

readings.title: The Bag with Holes
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH exposes the futility of extracting wealth for personal estates while the central mechanism of His presence lies in ruins.
readings.text: [Haggai 1:1] In the second year of Dareyavesh the sovereign, in the sixth new moon, on the first day of the new moon, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came by Ḥaggai the prophet to Zerubbaḇel son of She’alti’ěl, governor of Yehuḏah, and to Yehoshua son of Yehotsaḏaq, the high priest, saying, [2] <dq>“Thus spoke <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, saying, ‘This people have said, “The time has not come, the time the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to be built.” ’ ”</dq> [3] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came by Ḥaggai the prophet, saying, [4] <dq>“Is it time for you yourselves to dwell in your panelled houses, and this House be in ruins?”</dq> [5] <dq>And now, thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, “Consider your ways! [6] “You have sown much, but brought in little; eat, but do not have enough; drink, but you are not filled with drink; clothe yourselves, but no one is warm; and he who earns wages, earns wages to put into a bag with holes.”</dq>

readings.title: Calling for the Drought
readings.subtitle: The biological and economic collapse of the land is directly tied to the people's misplaced systemic priorities.
readings.text: [7] <dq>Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, “Consider your ways! [8] Go up to the mountain, and you shall bring wood and build the House. And <dn>I</dn> will be pleased with it, and let <dn>Me</dn> be esteemed,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [9] <dq>“When you looked for much, then see, it came to little. And when you brought it home, <dn>I</dn> would blow on it. Why?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. <dq>“Because of <dn>My</dn> House which lies in ruins, while each of you runs to his own house. [10] “Therefore the heavens above you have withheld the dew, and the earth has withheld its fruit. [11] “And <dn>I</dn> called for a drought on the land, and on the mountains, and on the grain, and on the new wine, and on the oil, and on whatever the ground brings forth, and on man, and on livestock, and on all the labour of the hands.”</dq>

readings.title: The Remnant Returns to Work
readings.subtitle: Realizing the authority of the prophetic word, the leaders and people re-engage the physical labor of the House.
readings.text: [Haggai 1:12] Then Zerubbaḇel son of She’alti’ěl, and Yehoshua son of Yehotsaḏaq, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the words of Ḥaggai the prophet, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> had sent him. And the people feared the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And Ḥaggai, the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, spoke the message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the people, saying, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am with you, declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stirred up <dn>את</dn> the spirit of Zerubbaḇel son of She’alti’ěl, governor of Yehuḏah, and <dn>את</dn> the spirit of Yehoshua son of Yehotsaḏaq, the high priest, and <dn>את</dn> the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and worked on the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, their <dn>Elohim</dn>, [15] on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth new moon, in the second year of Dareyavesh the sovereign.
